title: Micron Tech chipmaker union in Taiwan gets OK to strike
key_facts: The union at Micron's Taoyuan operation in Taiwan secured authorisation to strike, announced at a press conference in Taipei on 7 Oct 2026.
Of 2,258 eligible members, 2,012 voted over six days: 1,994 for, 14 against and four invalid ballots.
That is 88.3 percent of all eligible members, or 99 percent of those who voted.
No strike date is set; union chairman Jerry Lin said a 'surprise strike' is among the options and members would be told by text.
The dispute is over Micron's Incentive Pay Plan; the union wants 15 percent of operating profit distributed to employees.
Micron offered at least NT$1.7 million in cash compensation for fiscal 2026 in September, which the union rejected.
Micron says it respects workers' legal rights and will keep talking through mediation; Taiwan's Ministry of Labor urged 'concrete, feasible proposals'.
Micron's board meets on 8 to 9 Oct (US time); the union will wait for proposals before further action; a rally is set for Monday 19 Oct in Taipei.
quote_evidence: The result meant 88.3 percent of all eligible members backed a strike, or 99 percent of those who voted.

"We haven't decided on an actual strike schedule yet, but when the time comes, we will notify members by text message," Lin said, adding that a "surprise strike" was among the options being considered.
The Ministry of Labor said in a statement that it respected the union's strike vote, describing it as a reflection of employees' expectations for "a reasonable profit-sharing system."
why_it_matters_hint: A legal strike mandate now exists at Micron's Taiwan plant, but no date is set and talks continue.
